initiative.title: Art styles: lowpoly, painterly and photoreal zones
initiative.body: Every zone on the Verse is drawn in one of a few art styles, named in realms.json and defined by the engine: lowpoly, painterly (Breath of the Wild's look: soft toon bands, blue haze, painted skies, wind-swept grass) and photoreal. This initiative builds painterly in full and moves Everglade and Hecate's Cemetery onto it.

milestones.title: Zone styles: the field, the presets and the style fixture
milestones.body: A style per realm and zone, presets in verse/style.coax that realms declare rather than tune, and a fixture scene every feature shows on.

milestones.title: Painterly in the engine
milestones.body: Each element of the painterly look as an engine feature with the spec's numbers: bands, rim, tinted soft shadows, haze, sky, bloom and shafts, day and night, foliage, grass, painted packs, characters, water and light outlines. Needed by Hecate's Cemetery (Planetary Villa) and Everglade.

milestones.title: Painterly on phones, and the style check
milestones.body: The phone tier, and a release check that measures whether a painterly realm looks painterly, with a side-by-side sheet for the owner and Kiki.

milestones.title: Everglade in painterly
milestones.body: Everglade adopts the painterly preset and replaces what breaks the look: the grey haze, the bare ground, the grey-box people, the physical river, the plain stand-in boxes. Hecate's Cemetery's adoption is in the Planetary Villa project (https://openagents.com/projects/planetary-villa).

tasks.title: A style for every realm and zone in realms.json
tasks.body:
Add the required `style` field (lowpoly | painterly | photoreal), the optional `zones` list and the `clock` field (cycle | fixed:T | real) to realms.json. realms.ts writes them into realms.coax, the realm page (`data-style`) and the page facts (message 600: `style=`, `zone.<id>=`, `clock=`); `realms.ts --check` refuses a missing or unknown style, a duplicated zone id, and a painterly or photoreal realm whose WGSL lacks the generated style block. Tag every existing realm: Hecate's Cemetery and Everglade painterly (Hecate's `clock: fixed:0.0`, Everglade `cycle`), every other realm lowpoly. Pages accept `?clock=T` to pin the clock for shots. Nothing draws differently yet.

Specification: `docs/verse/art-styles.md`, The style field.

Needed by Hecate's Cemetery (Planetary Villa, https://openagents.com/projects/planetary-villa): hc-paint-tag; Everglade: eg-paint-pack. Those tasks wait on this one.
acceptance: `bun coax/web/realms.ts --check` passes on the tagged table and fails on each refusal case (a test per case)
Every realm page's facts carry its style and clock (headless shot with `--eval` reading them, or a host test)
docs/verse/realm-host.md documents the fields
Every realm's golden is unchanged

tasks.title: Style presets in the engine: verse/style.coax
tasks.body:
`verse/style.coax`: the `StylePreset` record with every painterly number in the spec (band edges and softness, rim, shadow tint, ambient, haze per clock key, sky, bloom, shafts, grass, foliage, water, tone, phone tier), the lowpoly preset (what realms draw today: one light term, light fog, no post) and a photoreal placeholder that refuses to evaluate. `verse_style_preset(style, tier)` and `verse_style_at(preset, clock)` (linear between the midnight, dawn, noon and dusk keys) fill a `STYLE_FLOATS` uniform block (32 vec4f). The shading functions are written in the subset `coax/web/wgsl.py` lowers and emitted into a realm's WGSL between `// ---- generated: verse/style.coax` markers; the band, rim, tint, haze and tone functions land here as stubs with their checks, and the feature tasks fill them.

Specification: `docs/verse/art-styles.md`, Presets.

Needed by Hecate's Cemetery (Planetary Villa, https://openagents.com/projects/planetary-villa): hc-paint-tag; Everglade: eg-paint-light. Those tasks wait on this one.
acceptance: coax test passes on every Coax file touched, with #test checks pinning the numbers the spec gives
`wgsl.py verse/style.coax ... --into` emits the block into the fixture's WGSL and it compiles in headless Chrome
The clock interpolation is checked at every key and halfway between
No realm changes look

tasks.title: The style fixture: a painterly test scene in the fixture realm
tasks.body:
The fixture realm, opened with `?style=painterly`, draws a fixed test scene in the preset: a sphere and a cube, a blob tree, a patch of grass, a small pond, a standing figure, and three ridges stepping back at 60, 140 and 260 m, from a fixed camera, at `?clock=0`, `0.25`, `0.5` and `0.75`. Without the query it draws exactly what it draws now, so its golden holds. Every engine task in this initiative shows its feature here and updates these goldens. Its golden name is `fixture-painterly-<clock>.png`.

tasks.title: Soft toon shading: three blended light bands, smooth normals
tasks.body:
The painterly diffuse: wrapped Lambert (wrap 0.25), the shadow term applied before banding, three bands (0, 0.55, 1.0) with edges at 0.20 and 0.58 and softness 0.06; two bands (edge 0.40, softness 0.08) for characters; no specular on matte surfaces and the one hard dab (step 0.92, 0.35) for wet or metal ones. Smooth vertex normals; the height field's normal blurred over 3 cells. In verse/style.coax, emitted to WGSL.

Specification: `docs/verse/art-styles.md`, 1. Shading.

Needed by Hecate's Cemetery (Planetary Villa, https://openagents.com/projects/planetary-villa): hc-paint-light; Everglade: eg-paint-light. Those tasks wait on this one.

Inside the frame budget of every realm that uses it, desktop and phone (measured, numbers in a note)

tasks.title: Warm rim light along silhouettes
tasks.body:
The rim term: `smoothstep(0.38, 0.12, N·V)` weighted toward the key light's side, strength 0.30 (world) and 0.45 (characters), colour by clock (day warm, dusk orange, night moon-silver at 0.6). It fogs with the surface and never draws over the sky.

tasks.title: Real soft shadows, tinted blue and violet, with a bright ambient
tasks.body:
Painterly realms draw a shadow map from the key light (the host's `shadow_vs`/`shadow_fs` path, 2048² desktop and 1024² phone, as the Haunted House uses): 9-tap Poisson PCF at 2.5 texels on desktop, 4 taps on a phone, fed into the bands. The shadow band takes `shadow_tint` (blue the largest channel, none under 0.35) and the hemisphere ambient by clock. Blob shadows stay under movers at 0.35 as contact shadows. A realm gives the shadow pass its draws; the light's frustum fits the camera's near 60 m (40 m on a phone).

tasks.title: The painterly post pass: tone curve, lifted blacks, gentle bloom
tasks.body:

Emissive materials keep writing their bloom share. The post functions live in verse/style.coax and are emitted.

tasks.title: Time of day: the clock, the sun's path, the moon as key at night
tasks.body:
`verse_style_at` drives the key light from the realm's clock: the sun's elevation from −20° at midnight to 60° at noon on the preset's azimuth; below −6° the moon is the key (0.35, (0.62, 0.70, 0.95)); key colour and strength by clock (day (1.00, 0.95, 0.85) 1.0, dusk/dawn (1.00, 0.72, 0.48) 0.75). A realm with its own moon (Hecate's) passes its direction and keeps the preset's colours. `cycle` turns once every 48 real minutes; `?clock=` pins it.

tasks.title: Blue-cyan distance haze that stacks ridges like painted flats
tasks.body:
The haze curve: `1 - exp(-density·max(d - start, 0))`, thinned with height (falloff 60/50/40 m), capped (0.88/0.88/0.85), its colour per clock key from the spec's table and warmed toward the key light by `pow(V·L, 8)·0.45`. Applied identically to every surface, water, grass and particles; the sky's horizon equals the haze colour. Phone density ×1.25.

tasks.title: The painted sky: gradient, sun or moon with halo, soft clouds, night
tasks.body:

A realm with its own moon keeps it (Hecate's real phase).

tasks.title: Dense wind-swept grass that sways constantly
tasks.body:
GPU-instanced grass blades from a hash of their cell (no blade buffer): 0.35 to 0.60 m tapered triangles, 24 per m² out to 32 m on desktop, 8 per m² out to 18 m on a phone, shrinking to nothing over the last 6 m. Colour from the ground's painted colour, tips 15% lighter and warmer, ±4% hue jitter, normals the ground's up. Wind: `A(0.6 sin(k·x − ωt) + 0.4 gust)`, A 0.30 rad, wavelength 12 m, 3 m/s, bend by height², bright bands rolling across; blades within 0.7 m of up to 8 movers lean away. The realm supplies the mask (paths, squares, floors, water, plots) as capsules plus its path distance. Frozen at t = 0 under `still`. The wind function is shared with foliage sway.

tasks.title: Blob-shaded canopies: sphere-ish normals, sway, matching far trees
tasks.body:
A canopy's normal becomes `normalize(mix(mesh_n, normalize(p - c), 0.85))` with `c` from the pack catalog's bounds (an ellipsoid for pines and cypresses) or a primitive's centre; leaf cards keep their alpha cut. Canopies sway with the grass wind at 0.05 m times their relative height. Far-tree cones shade with the same normal and colour as the kit tree they stand for. The pack's catalog gives each `_Leaves` mesh a canopy flag (pack_realm.py).

tasks.title: Painted texture packs: pack style, texture rules, the paint pass and the release check
tasks.body:
Packs declare `"style"`; pack_realm.py writes `style NAME` into the catalog and checks painterly layers: at most 512 texels (256 default for props and characters), no normal/roughness/detail maps, fine-detail energy ≤ 0.035 (luminance minus its 4×-down-up copy, RMS over opaque texels), saturation and value inside the albedo rules. `"paint": true` runs the paint pass (Kuwahara r4/r2, 24-colour quantize, saturation pulled into range) and the result must pass. `realms.ts --check` and the release walk refuse a realm whose pack's style differs from its own. The licences file is unchanged in shape.

Specification: `docs/verse/art-styles.md`, 10. Textures and packs.

Needed by Everglade: eg-paint-pack, eg-paint-people. Those tasks wait on this one.

tasks.title: Painterly characters: two bands, strong rim, flat skin and cloth
tasks.body:
Skinned and figure characters take the character shading: two bands (edge 0.40, softness 0.08), rim 0.45, the tinted shadow and the cast shadow, no specular, textures sampled with LOD bias +2 at 512 texels so fine grain goes. Emissive materials (Hecate's dog) and designed blacks (the shadow visitor) are exempt by material flag. The pack's character layers go through the painterly checks. verse/skin.coax and verse/figure.coax consumers get the same functions.

tasks.title: A stylized water preset: colour bands and sparkles
tasks.body:
A `painted` preset in verse/water-look.coax beside the seven physical ones, with its shader path: depth colour bands (shallow under 0.4 m, mid to 1.5 m, deep, edges soft over 0.15 m) in place of Beer-Lambert; the sky gradient reflected with Schlick Fresnel and no roughness blur; sparkles on a 0.15 m grid (0.25 m phone) within 4° of the key light, 2 to 3 px, twinkling over 0.3 s, in place of GGX glints; a clean 0.25 m shore line and W6's ripples as white rings; haze and tone as every surface. The physics (W1), the mesh and the swimmer are unchanged; `water_body_sample` and the swimmer checks still pass.

tasks.title: The style check: measure "looks painterly" and the side-by-side sheet
tasks.body:
`coax/web/style-check.ts URL --style painterly`: shoots each painterly realm's `style_views` (realms.json) headless at 1440×900 and 390×844 with the clock pinned and `still`, masks the HUD plates, and measures fine detail (≤ 0.035), dark ink (≤ 0.2%), near black (≤ 0.5% day, ≤ 2% night), shadow hue (blue ≥ red, green), mean saturation (0.22 to 0.60), haze (ΔE ≤ 12 from the preset, spread ≤ 0.08) and bands (two peaks on the largest lit object, via `?probe`). It writes `style-<slug>.png`, the realm's views beside the style fixture's, for the owner's and Kiki's judgment. goldens.ts runs it for every painterly realm in the release walk; a failure stops the release.

tasks.title: Everglade: painterly light, haze, sky and a day that turns
